questions.question: The radius is homologous to which bone of the lower limb?
questions.explanation: The text states the radius is homologous to the medial bone of the leg, the tibia.

questions.question: Which of the following is a part of the radius?
questions.explanation: The radius consists of three parts: upper end, shaft, and lower end.

questions.question: Which structure is located at the upper end of the radius?
questions.explanation: The upper end presents the head, neck, and radial tuberosity.

questions.question: The head of the radius articulates superiorly with which structure?
questions.explanation: The head is disc shaped and articulates above with the capitulum of the humerus.

questions.question: Where is the radial tuberosity located?
questions.explanation: The radial tuberosity is just below the medial part of the neck.

questions.question: What is the shape of the radial head?
questions.explanation: The text describes the head of the radius as disc shaped.

questions.question: Which border of the radius is the sharpest?
questions.explanation: The medial or interosseous border is described as the sharpest border.

questions.question: How many surfaces does the lower end of the radius present?
questions.explanation: The lower end of the radius is the widest part and presents five surfaces.

questions.question: Which structure projects distally from the lateral surface of the lower end of the radius?
questions.explanation: The lateral surface of the lower end projects distally as the styloid process.

questions.question: Which palpable structure is located on the dorsal surface of the lower end of the radius?
questions.explanation: The dorsal surface presents a palpable dorsal tubercle known as Lister's tubercle.

questions.question: What limits the dorsal tubercle of the radius medially?
questions.explanation: The dorsal tubercle is limited medially by an oblique groove.

questions.question: In determining the side of the radius, which direction should the narrow disc-shaped end face?
questions.explanation: The narrow disc-shaped end (head) should be directed upwards.

questions.question: When determining the side of the radius, where should the sharpest border be kept?
questions.explanation: The sharpest interosseous border of the shaft is kept medially.

questions.question: Which structure encircles the circumference of the radial head?
questions.explanation: The rest of the circumference of the head is encircled by the annular ligament.

questions.question: Which ligament is attached to the medial side of the radial neck?
questions.explanation: The quadrate ligament is attached to the medial side of the neck.

questions.question: Which structure is inserted into the rough posterior part of the radial tuberosity?
questions.explanation: The biceps tendon is inserted to the rough posterior part of the radial tuberosity.

questions.question: What covers the smooth anterior part of the radial tuberosity?
questions.explanation: A small synovial bursa covers its smooth anterior part and separates it from the biceps tendon.

questions.question: Which border of the radius is well-defined only in its middle third?
questions.explanation: The posterior border is well-defined only in its middle third of the shaft.

questions.question: What is the upper part of the anterior border of the radius called?
questions.explanation: The upper part of the anterior border is called the anterior oblique line.

questions.question: Which muscle originates from the anterior oblique line of the radius?
questions.explanation: The anterior oblique line gives origin to the radial head of flexor digitorum superficialis.

questions.question: Which membrane is attached to the lower three-fourths of the medial border of the radius?
questions.explanation: The interosseous membrane is attached to its lower three-fourth.

questions.question: Which muscle originates from the upper two-fourths of the anterior surface of the radius?
questions.explanation: Flexor pollicis longus originates from the upper two-fourth of the anterior surface.

questions.question: Which muscle is inserted on the lower one-fourth of the anterior surface of the radius?
questions.explanation: Pronator quadratus is inserted on the lower one-fourth of the anterior surface.

questions.question: In which direction is the nutrient canal on the anterior surface of the radius directed?
questions.explanation: The nutrient canal on the anterior surface is directed upwards.

questions.question: The nutrient artery for the radius is a branch of which artery?
questions.explanation: The nutrient artery for the radius is a branch from the anterior interosseous artery.

questions.question: Which muscle arises from the middle one-third of the posterior surface of the radius?
questions.explanation: Abductor pollicis longus arises from the middle one-third of the posterior surface.

questions.question: Which muscle arises from the lower part of the posterior surface of the radius?
questions.explanation: Extensor pollicis brevis arises from the lower part of the posterior surface.

questions.question: Which muscle is inserted on the widened upper one-third of the lateral surface of the radius?
questions.explanation: Supinator is inserted on the widened upper one-third of the lateral surface.

questions.question: Which muscle is inserted on the rough area in the most convex middle part of the lateral surface of the radius?
questions.explanation: Pronator teres is inserted on the rough area in the most convex middle part of the lateral surface.

questions.question: Which structure forms the posterior oblique line of the radius?
options: Lower part of the medial border
Upper part of the posterior border
Lateral part of the anterior border
Middle part of the interosseous border
questions.explanation: Above, the posterior border runs upwards and medially to the radial tuberosity and forms the posterior oblique line.
